# Disagreement Log — Apocalypse of Peter, Chapter 9
**Agents:** EMET | LOGOS | PNEUMA
**Total Disagreements:** 11

---

## Verse-by-Verse Disagreements

### v.1 — "I beheld" vs. "I saw" vs. "I saw... fire flowing past their mouths" (PNEUMA)
- **EMET/LOGOS:** "I beheld"
- **PNEUMA:** "I saw... fire flowing past their mouths, lapping at their faces"
- **Note:** PNEUMA adds vivid physical description not in source. "Beheld" vs. "saw" is minor but EMET/LOGOS's "beheld" preserves a more formal visionary register.

### v.3 — "did not have righteousness in their hearts"
- **EMET:** "did not have righteousness in their hearts, but instead worked iniquity"
- **LOGOS:** "had no righteousness in their hearts but worked iniquity instead"
- **PNEUMA:** "had no righteousness in them... full of wickedness and nothing else"
- **Note:** PNEUMA's "nothing else" is an addition. The contrast between "no righteousness" and "worked iniquity" is preserved by EMET/LOGOS.

### v.5 — "made music for the pleasures of the world"
- All agents retain the phrase. PNEUMA adds "Entertainers — they used their art."
- **Note:** PNEUMA's "Entertainers" is an interpretive label not in source. "Used their art" is an addition.

### v.6 — "covered in dust" vs. "gray with dust"
- **EMET/LOGOS:** "covered in dust"
- **PNEUMA:** "gray with dust"
- **Note:** Minor. "Gray with dust" is more vivid; "covered in dust" is more literal.

### v.7 — "had riches in the world" vs. "hoarded what they had" (PNEUMA)
- **EMET:** "had riches in the world"
- **LOGOS:** "had riches in this world"
- **PNEUMA:** "hoarded what they had"
- **Note:** "Hoarded" is PNEUMA's significant interpretive addition — the source simply says they had riches and trusted in them.

### v.7 — "treated God's commandments with contempt" (PNEUMA)
- **EMET/LOGOS:** "despised the commandments of God"
- **PNEUMA:** "treated God's commandments with contempt"
- **Note:** Equivalent in meaning but PNEUMA's phrasing loses "despised" (*kataphronein*).

### v.8 — "discharging filth and blood"
- All agents retain this. PNEUMA adds "breathing through filth" — not in source.
- **Note:** PNEUMA's addition makes explicit what the submersion implies but oversteps the text.

### v.10 — "gave themselves up to fornication" vs. "gave themselves entirely to fornication" (PNEUMA)
- **EMET:** "given themselves up to fornication"
- **LOGOS:** "gave themselves over to fornication"
- **PNEUMA:** "gave themselves entirely to fornication"
- **Note:** "Entirely" is PNEUMA's intensifier. "Given themselves over" (LOGOS) is most natural.

### v.11 — "suspended over the water by their tongues" vs. "dangling over the water, hung by their own tongues"
- **EMET:** "hanged up over the water by their tongues"
- **LOGOS:** "suspended over the water by their tongues"
- **PNEUMA:** "dangling over the water, hung by their own tongues"
- **Note:** Minor differences; all convey the image. "Hanged up" (EMET) is archaic.

### v.13 — "blasphemed the way of righteousness"
- All agents retain. The self-quotation is reproduced identically. No disagreement on v.13 itself.

### v.15 — "the outer darkness"
- All three agents agree. No disagreement.
- **Note:** PNEUMA adds extensive commentary in the note, but the translation line is identical across agents.

---
*11 disagreements. SOPHIA: retain "beheld" register (v.1); reject "hoarded" (v.7); reject "breathing through filth" addition (v.8); prefer "gave themselves over" (v.10).*
